Sentence (English): This is my first time buying a dishwasher.
Comments (English): [ This is my first time buying a dishwasher. Since my house isn't very big, I was most concerned about the size. Then, I heard Minix had a mini dishwasher, so I ordered one! I'm really happy with the size! The design is also cute and adorable. ] || ---------------- || This is my first time buying a dishwasher. My house isn't very big, so size was my biggest concern. Then, I heard Minix had a mini dishwasher, so I ordered it! I'm really happy with the size! The design is cute and looks great, too. However, the product description said gray. I thought it was white, but it's a bit more gray than I expected. Keep that in mind! After using it for two days, the noise isn't that loud, but it was a bit irritating for me because I have sensitive ears. However, if I watch TV or use the computer while it's running, the noise naturally drowns it out, so I don't really care. I was a little taken aback by the cleaning power at first. I tested it on the quick cycle with a bunch of dishes, but it didn't clean very well. I was really surprised, but after I arranged the dishes properly and ran it on the standard cycle, they came out completely clean and sterilized, which was a huge plus. I was amazed at how old grime that had previously been difficult to remove by hand was completely removed in one cycle. I think you really need to arrange the dishes carefully to get the best cleaning results. Even though it's mini-sized, if you arrange them neatly like Tetris, it secretly holds a lot of dishes. It's not small. Assuming they don't eat that much, I think it can serve up to 4 people. Lastly, water! It definitely uses less water than washing dishes by hand, so it seems economical. Especially when you wash dishes by hand, you usually run hot water, right? That's really wasteful, but this one uses exactly the amount of water it needs, so it feels like it's saving money. I talked nonsense as I used it, but in the end, I'm very satisfied! I recommend it~

Sentence (English): The Nature Beige color looks natural and pretty.
Comments (English): [ Why did I only buy this now? ] || ---------------- || The Nature Beige color looks natural and pretty. Since my parents' house is an old building, I took the opportunity to replace the faucet and sink drain pipes while I was at it, along with installing the dishwasher. Because it's a wall-mounted faucet, they drilled a hole in the countertop to connect it. I heard that Samsung dishwashers can't be installed with wall-mounted faucets, so I only looked at LG from the start. I chose a product that seemed to offer good value for money. It has all the features I was looking for, so I'm satisfied with it. Actually, I think the most important feature is the automatic door opening function. It seems like this feature is available on models 12 place settings or larger. I mainly use the automatic or 1-hour + high-temperature drying functions. The dishes wash well, and although this is my first time using a 12-place setting dishwasher, the interior is spacious and nice. Large pots fit well too. It's sufficient to run it just once in the evening after gathering the dishes, but the top-loading quick wash function is also great for when I want to wash dishes immediately.

Sentence (English): Purchased the dish washer (dw) within the past two weeks and have used just two or three times.
Comments (English): [ Overall satisfied - some things you should know ] || ---------------- || Purchased the dish washer (dw) within the past two weeks and have used just two or three times. It is working well including the heated dry. Normal cycle takes a very long time (> 3 hours). Quick wash about half that. Apparently the longer times are common for newer units due to energy savings.Unit sits closer to the floor meaning the door opens further down, thus you need to bend over further.The bottom dish rack rolls almost too easily in the stainless steel cabinet. Utensil rack moves back and forth within the bottom rack.Installed the dw myself. Note that because the dw sits closer to the floor, you MUST adjust the rear legs before moving it into the surrounding cabinet. You will not be able to reach them later. My kitchen's floor is ceramic tile and is raised up in front of the dishwasher. That made installation very challenging even after temporarily raising the laminated counter top. One of the final steps requires reinserting a connector and reinstalling a drip tray. In my case it was VERY difficult. It would have been helpful if the wires for the connector were just a little longer.

Comments (English): [ Garbage product, destroyed floors ] || ---------------- || Like many of the other reviews, dishwasher started leaking after roughly two and a half years of use. We came home to find the dishwasher had started leaking and flooded our hallway and living room wood floors behind our kitchen. Wood floors and partial cabinetry are now ruined. Completely unsatisfied with GE's response. Originally had a diagnosis by a local home builder that there was a cracked pump/motor causing the leak and advised to purchase a new dishwasher. After reaching out to GE, we were told they'd waive the fee to send out a technician to diagnose the problem, but we'd be responsible for repairs. We were also given a contact for their insurance for property damage. We decided to have the GE tech come out to diagnose the dishwasher to help support the property damage claim. We were contacted by the tech the day prior to coming out, and were told he wouldn't come out unless we planned on fixing the dishwasher. Paid $300 for the repair of the cracked motor/pump. Complained to GE who offered to reimburse us for $100 of the repair, and they also emphasized that the repair may not even solve the problem. Paid nearly $1,500 for a dishwasher and professional installation that caused upwards of $10,000 - $30,000 in property damage, and GE's response to my request for reimbursement of the $300 repair is to reimburse a measly $100. Expensive, poor quality product and even worse customer service. Hoping we can at least recover compensation through insurance for the property damage caused by the dishwasher. Thanks GE.

Ultimately, I was very satisfied with the quality and design, and the product was a good value for money. However, the only drawback was the service, which was different from other brands. They brought out a ton of boxes and trash, and told me to clean them up. They barely explained how to operate the system. I think they were busy, but it was unavoidable that the installers from other brands came. This is a bit of a hit-or-miss situation, so if you want a clean installation, friendly service, and guidance, I recommend giving this one some thought! If you found this helpful, please like it. Sentence (English): This 12-seater Media dishwasher.
Comments (English): [ It's a good value product. ] || ---------------- || This 12-seater Media dishwasher. While preparing for my new home, this was the first item I purchased among the "three aunts"—the dryer, dishwasher, and oven cleaner! This is my first time doing household chores, but I prefer to keep things as simple as possible. The dishwasher is truly a perfect fit! We're a newlywed couple, living in a two-person household. We store our breakfast and lunch in a stainless steel bowl and run it once in the evening. I was debating between a 6-seater and a 12-seater, but I heard the 12-seater has a more powerful motor. The fact that I could get a 12-seater for the price of a 6-seater from another brand was a plus. Also, since it's a brand that supplies to a well-known company, I thought it had some recognition for its dishwashers. So, while I'd purchased all my other appliances from L, I chose Media for the dishwasher. While it's not as well-known in Korea, it's a fairly popular brand overseas. Since Holland is the brand's model, my husband, a soccer fan, trusted me. Ultimately, I'm very satisfied with the overall quality, design, and value for money. However, the only downside is that the service is different from other brands. Reviews say the service is excellent and friendly, so I trusted them and purchased this product. However, I was assigned a very rude installer, which was actually quite stressful. They brought out huge boxes and trash, and told me to clean them up. They barely explained how to operate the product. I guess they were busy, but I couldn't help but compare it to other brands' installers. This part seems a bit hit and miss, so if you want a clean installation, friendly service, and guidance, you might want to give this one some thought! If you found this review helpful, please give it a like. This is a review I paid for myself!

Hello, I am a housewife of 10 years raising a 40-month-old child and a member of a 3-person household. I have used this for a year and am finally leaving a review now. However, I do feel a bit uneasy about baby bottles, children's tableware, and straws, so I use the 'Baby Bottle Sterilization Mode' to gather all the straw cups and wash them every three days. Also, having a separate basket for cutlery is definitely a plus. I've never had anything fly off. Does it increase water bills? = My water bill dropped significantly after using the dishwasher. People usually use a lot of water to wash dishes thoroughly, but since the dishwasher is consistent, the bill actually decreases. How to clean the dishwasher: I put citric acid in the detergent dispenser and run it on the drum wash cycle. I remove the filter at the bottom, soak it in warm water, and then clean it with a toothbrush. It keeps things clean and isn't difficult. I haven't bought any separate cleaning detergent. Another good point is that if you get extra dishes in the middle of the cycle, you can stop it, open the lid, and put them in. (Please refer to the photo; water doesn't leak.) Also, there is an automatic opening function, so it stays slightly open after the cycle is finished, allowing for natural drying. I tend to open it completely to dry. After using it for a year, I realized that even the parts I initially considered downsides are actually strengths. I am still very satisfied and using it well. If my review was helpful, please give it a thumbs up.

Does it dry? = When I bought it, I thought it dried immediately after washing, but that wasn't the case. Since I'm not going to use it right away anyway, I just leave it completely open and let it dry on its own, so I haven't really needed the drying function and have been using it well for a year. However, I do feel a bit uneasy about baby bottles, children's tableware, and straws, so I use the 'Baby Bottle Sterilization Mode' to gather all the straw cups and wash them every three days. Is it convenient? = For a year, the only dishwashing I do is frying pans. I run everything, stainless steel and all. I bought it for convenience, and I am completely satisfied. It’s perfect for a household of three. Even though I have a lot of dishes to wash, I run it about twice a day. I've never run it more than three times; it's usually twice. Also, having a separate basket for cutlery is definitely a plus. I've never had anything fly off. Does it increase water bills? = My water bill dropped significantly after using the dishwasher. People usually use a lot of water to wash dishes thoroughly, but since the dishwasher is consistent, the bill actually decreases. How to clean the dishwasher: I put citric acid in the detergent dispenser and run it on the drum wash cycle. I remove the filter at the bottom, soak it in warm water, and then clean it with a toothbrush. It keeps things clean and isn't difficult. I haven't bought any separate cleaning detergent. Another good point is that if you get extra dishes in the middle of the cycle, you can stop it, open the lid, and put them in. (Please refer to the photo; water doesn't leak.) Also, there is an automatic opening function, so it stays slightly open after the cycle is finished, allowing for natural drying. I tend to open it completely to dry. After using it for a year, I realized that even the parts I initially considered downsides are actually strengths. I am still very satisfied and using it well. If my review was helpful, please give it a thumbs up.

Also, there is an automatic opening function, so it stays slightly open after the cycle is finished, allowing for natural drying. I tend to open it completely to dry. After using it for a year, I realized that even the parts I initially considered downsides are actually strengths. I am still very satisfied and using it well. If my review was helpful, please give it a thumbs up.

After using it for a year, I realized that even the parts I initially considered downsides are actually strengths. I am still very satisfied and using it well. If my review was helpful, please give it a thumbs up.

Hello, I am a housewife of 10 years raising a 40-month-old child and a member of a 3-person household. I have used this for a year and am finally leaving a review now. However, buying a large dishwasher wasn't an option because our kitchen is on the smaller side, and built-in models were out of the question. So, I did a lot of searching online. Based on my consideration and experience, here is the conclusion: Does it clean well? = I wanted to put everything in at once and wash it thoroughly. As shown in the picture, I always load a lot of items for washing, and it cleans up nicely. Previously, I used a basket, but it felt like straws weren't getting cleaned properly. However, when I put the straws directly into the existing dishwasher, they actually cleaned much better. Even if you pack everything like Tetris, it cleans sufficiently well. Design. What more needs to be said? It’s not that big, and the color is lovely pink. I’ve been using it for a year, and it’s so pretty with its glossy finish and not a single scratch. Visitors who see it in person also say how beautiful it is and ask if it’s really a dishwasher. Does it dry? = When I bought it, I thought it dried immediately after washing, but that wasn't the case. Instead, there is a separate drying mode, but it doesn't dry things completely and feels a bit iffy. Since I'm not going to use it right away anyway, I just leave it completely open and let it dry on its own, so I haven't really needed the drying function and have been using it well for a year. However, I do feel a bit uneasy about baby bottles, children's tableware, and straws, so I use the 'Baby Bottle Sterilization Mode' to gather all the straw cups and wash them every three days. Is it convenient? = For a year, the only dishwashing I do is frying pans. I run everything, stainless steel and all. I bought it for convenience, and I am completely satisfied. It’s perfect for a household of three. Even though I have a lot of dishes to wash, I run it about twice a day. I've never run it more than three times; it's usually twice. Also, having a separate basket for cutlery is definitely a plus. I've never had anything fly off. Does it increase water bills? = My water bill dropped significantly after using the dishwasher. People usually use a lot of water to wash dishes thoroughly, but since the dishwasher is consistent, the bill actually decreases. How to clean the dishwasher: I put citric acid in the detergent dispenser and run it on the drum wash cycle. I remove the filter at the bottom, soak it in warm water, and then clean it with a toothbrush. It keeps things clean and isn't difficult. I haven't bought any separate cleaning detergent. Another good point is that if you get extra dishes in the middle of the cycle, you can stop it, open the lid, and put them in. (Please refer to the photo; water doesn't leak.) Also, there is an automatic opening function, so it stays slightly open after the cycle is finished, allowing for natural drying. I tend to open it completely to dry. After using it for a year, I realized that even the parts I initially considered downsides are actually strengths. I am still very satisfied and using it well. If my review was helpful, please give it a thumbs up.

Comments (English): [ 1-Year Usage Review ] || ---------------- || 1-Year Usage Review. Purchase Date: April 30, 2024. Hello, I am a housewife of 10 years raising a 40-month-old child and a member of a 3-person household. I have used this for a year and am finally leaving a review now. This is an honest review based on my own purchase and long-term use. First, although we graduated from baby bottles a long time ago, washing straw cups was too difficult. As my child grew, dishes, water bottles, and bowls piled up so much that washing dishes became a major chore. However, buying a large dishwasher wasn't an option because our kitchen is on the smaller side, and built-in models were out of the question. So, I did a lot of searching online. Based on my consideration and experience, here is the conclusion: Does it clean well? = I wanted to put everything in at once and wash it thoroughly. As shown in the picture, I always load a lot of items for washing, and it cleans up nicely. Previously, I used a basket, but it felt like straws weren't getting cleaned properly. However, when I put the straws directly into the existing dishwasher, they actually cleaned much better. Even if you pack everything like Tetris, it cleans sufficiently well. Design. What more needs to be said? It’s not that big, and the color is lovely pink. I’ve been using it for a year, and it’s so pretty with its glossy finish and not a single scratch. Visitors who see it in person also say how beautiful it is and ask if it’s really a dishwasher. Does it dry? = When I bought it, I thought it dried immediately after washing, but that wasn't the case. Instead, there is a separate drying mode, but it doesn't dry things completely and feels a bit iffy. Since I'm not going to use it right away anyway, I just leave it completely open and let it dry on its own, so I haven't really needed the drying function and have been using it well for a year. However, I do feel a bit uneasy about baby bottles, children's tableware, and straws, so I use the 'Baby Bottle Sterilization Mode' to gather all the straw cups and wash them every three days. Is it convenient? = For a year, the only dishwashing I do is frying pans. I run everything, stainless steel and all. I bought it for convenience, and I am completely satisfied. It’s perfect for a household of three. Even though I have a lot of dishes to wash, I run it about twice a day. I've never run it more than three times; it's usually twice. Also, having a separate basket for cutlery is definitely a plus. I've never had anything fly off. Does it increase water bills? = My water bill dropped significantly after using the dishwasher. People usually use a lot of water to wash dishes thoroughly, but since the dishwasher is consistent, the bill actually decreases. How to clean the dishwasher: I put citric acid in the detergent dispenser and run it on the drum wash cycle. I remove the filter at the bottom, soak it in warm water, and then clean it with a toothbrush. It keeps things clean and isn't difficult. I haven't bought any separate cleaning detergent. Another good point is that if you get extra dishes in the middle of the cycle, you can stop it, open the lid, and put them in. (Please refer to the photo; water doesn't leak.) Also, there is an automatic opening function, so it stays slightly open after the cycle is finished, allowing for natural drying. I tend to open it completely to dry. After using it for a year, I realized that even the parts I initially considered downsides are actually strengths. I am still very satisfied and using it well. If my review was helpful, please give it a thumbs up.

Comments (English): [ 1-Year Usage Review ] || ---------------- || 1-Year Usage Review. Purchase Date: April 30, 2024. Hello, I am a housewife of 10 years raising a 40-month-old child and a member of a 3-person household. I have used this for a year and am finally leaving a review now. This is an honest review based on my own purchase and long-term use. First, although we graduated from baby bottles a long time ago, washing straw cups was too difficult. As my child grew, dishes, water bottles, and bowls piled up so much that washing dishes became a major chore. However, buying a large dishwasher wasn't an option because our kitchen is on the smaller side, and built-in models were out of the question. So, I did a lot of searching online. Based on my consideration and experience, here is the conclusion: Does it clean well? = I wanted to put everything in at once and wash it thoroughly. As shown in the picture, I always load a lot of items for washing, and it cleans up nicely. Previously, I used a basket, but it felt like straws weren't getting cleaned properly. However, when I put the straws directly into the existing dishwasher, they actually cleaned much better. Even if you pack everything like Tetris, it cleans sufficiently well. Design. What more needs to be said? It’s not that big, and the color is lovely pink. I’ve been using it for a year, and it’s so pretty with its glossy finish and not a single scratch. Visitors who see it in person also say how beautiful it is and ask if it’s really a dishwasher. Does it dry? = When I bought it, I thought it dried immediately after washing, but that wasn't the case. Instead, there is a separate drying mode, but it doesn't dry things completely and feels a bit iffy. Since I'm not going to use it right away anyway, I just leave it completely open and let it dry on its own, so I haven't really needed the drying function and have been using it well for a year. However, I do feel a bit uneasy about baby bottles, children's tableware, and straws, so I use the 'Baby Bottle Sterilization Mode' to gather all the straw cups and wash them every three days. Is it convenient? = For a year, the only dishwashing I do is frying pans. I run everything, stainless steel and all. I bought it for convenience, and I am completely satisfied. It’s perfect for a household of three. Even though I have a lot of dishes to wash, I run it about twice a day. I've never run it more than three times; it's usually twice. Also, having a separate basket for cutlery is definitely a plus. I've never had anything fly off. Does it increase water bills? = My water bill dropped significantly after using the dishwasher. People usually use a lot of water to wash dishes thoroughly, but since the dishwasher is consistent, the bill actually decreases. How to clean the dishwasher: I put citric acid in the detergent dispenser and run it on the drum wash cycle. I remove the filter at the bottom, soak it in warm water, and then clean it with a toothbrush. It keeps things clean and isn't difficult. I haven't bought any separate cleaning detergent. Another good point is that if you get extra dishes in the middle of the cycle, you can stop it, open the lid, and put them in. (Please refer to the photo; water doesn't leak.) Also, there is an automatic opening function, so it stays slightly open after the cycle is finished, allowing for natural drying. I tend to open it completely to dry. After using it for a year, I realized that even the parts I initially considered downsides are actually strengths. I am still very satisfied and using it well. If my review was helpful, please give it a thumbs up.

Comments (English): [ 1-Year Usage Review ] || ---------------- || 1-Year Usage Review. Purchase Date: April 30, 2024. Hello, I am a housewife of 10 years raising a 40-month-old child and a member of a 3-person household. I have used this for a year and am finally leaving a review now. This is an honest review based on my own purchase and long-term use. First, although we graduated from baby bottles a long time ago, washing straw cups was too difficult. As my child grew, dishes, water bottles, and bowls piled up so much that washing dishes became a major chore. However, buying a large dishwasher wasn't an option because our kitchen is on the smaller side, and built-in models were out of the question. So, I did a lot of searching online. Based on my consideration and experience, here is the conclusion: Does it clean well? = I wanted to put everything in at once and wash it thoroughly. As shown in the picture, I always load a lot of items for washing, and it cleans up nicely. Previously, I used a basket, but it felt like straws weren't getting cleaned properly. However, when I put the straws directly into the existing dishwasher, they actually cleaned much better. Even if you pack everything like Tetris, it cleans sufficiently well. Design. What more needs to be said? It’s not that big, and the color is lovely pink. I’ve been using it for a year, and it’s so pretty with its glossy finish and not a single scratch. Visitors who see it in person also say how beautiful it is and ask if it’s really a dishwasher. Does it dry? = When I bought it, I thought it dried immediately after washing, but that wasn't the case. Instead, there is a separate drying mode, but it doesn't dry things completely and feels a bit iffy. Since I'm not going to use it right away anyway, I just leave it completely open and let it dry on its own, so I haven't really needed the drying function and have been using it well for a year. However, I do feel a bit uneasy about baby bottles, children's tableware, and straws, so I use the 'Baby Bottle Sterilization Mode' to gather all the straw cups and wash them every three days. Is it convenient? = For a year, the only dishwashing I do is frying pans. I run everything, stainless steel and all. I bought it for convenience, and I am completely satisfied. It’s perfect for a household of three. Even though I have a lot of dishes to wash, I run it about twice a day. I've never run it more than three times; it's usually twice. Also, having a separate basket for cutlery is definitely a plus. I've never had anything fly off. Does it increase water bills? = My water bill dropped significantly after using the dishwasher. People usually use a lot of water to wash dishes thoroughly, but since the dishwasher is consistent, the bill actually decreases. How to clean the dishwasher: I put citric acid in the detergent dispenser and run it on the drum wash cycle. I remove the filter at the bottom, soak it in warm water, and then clean it with a toothbrush. It keeps things clean and isn't difficult. I haven't bought any separate cleaning detergent. Another good point is that if you get extra dishes in the middle of the cycle, you can stop it, open the lid, and put them in. (Please refer to the photo; water doesn't leak.) Also, there is an automatic opening function, so it stays slightly open after the cycle is finished, allowing for natural drying. I tend to open it completely to dry. After using it for a year, I realized that even the parts I initially considered downsides are actually strengths. I am still very satisfied and using it well. If my review was helpful, please give it a thumbs up.

Comments (English): [ 1-Year Usage Review ] || ---------------- || 1-Year Usage Review. Purchase Date: April 30, 2024. Hello, I am a housewife of 10 years raising a 40-month-old child and a member of a 3-person household. I have used this for a year and am finally leaving a review now. This is an honest review based on my own purchase and long-term use. First, although we graduated from baby bottles a long time ago, washing straw cups was too difficult. As my child grew, dishes, water bottles, and bowls piled up so much that washing dishes became a major chore. However, buying a large dishwasher wasn't an option because our kitchen is on the smaller side, and built-in models were out of the question. So, I did a lot of searching online. Based on my consideration and experience, here is the conclusion: Does it clean well? = I wanted to put everything in at once and wash it thoroughly. As shown in the picture, I always load a lot of items for washing, and it cleans up nicely. Previously, I used a basket, but it felt like straws weren't getting cleaned properly. However, when I put the straws directly into the existing dishwasher, they actually cleaned much better. Even if you pack everything like Tetris, it cleans sufficiently well. Design. What more needs to be said? It’s not that big, and the color is lovely pink. I’ve been using it for a year, and it’s so pretty with its glossy finish and not a single scratch. Visitors who see it in person also say how beautiful it is and ask if it’s really a dishwasher. Does it dry? = When I bought it, I thought it dried immediately after washing, but that wasn't the case. Instead, there is a separate drying mode, but it doesn't dry things completely and feels a bit iffy. Since I'm not going to use it right away anyway, I just leave it completely open and let it dry on its own, so I haven't really needed the drying function and have been using it well for a year. However, I do feel a bit uneasy about baby bottles, children's tableware, and straws, so I use the 'Baby Bottle Sterilization Mode' to gather all the straw cups and wash them every three days. Is it convenient? = For a year, the only dishwashing I do is frying pans. I run everything, stainless steel and all. I bought it for convenience, and I am completely satisfied. It’s perfect for a household of three. Even though I have a lot of dishes to wash, I run it about twice a day. I've never run it more than three times; it's usually twice. Also, having a separate basket for cutlery is definitely a plus. I've never had anything fly off. Does it increase water bills? = My water bill dropped significantly after using the dishwasher. People usually use a lot of water to wash dishes thoroughly, but since the dishwasher is consistent, the bill actually decreases. How to clean the dishwasher: I put citric acid in the detergent dispenser and run it on the drum wash cycle. I remove the filter at the bottom, soak it in warm water, and then clean it with a toothbrush. It keeps things clean and isn't difficult. I haven't bought any separate cleaning detergent. Another good point is that if you get extra dishes in the middle of the cycle, you can stop it, open the lid, and put them in. (Please refer to the photo; water doesn't leak.) Also, there is an automatic opening function, so it stays slightly open after the cycle is finished, allowing for natural drying. I tend to open it completely to dry. After using it for a year, I realized that even the parts I initially considered downsides are actually strengths. I am still very satisfied and using it well. If my review was helpful, please give it a thumbs up.

However, I do feel a bit uneasy about baby bottles, children's tableware, and straws, so I use the 'Baby Bottle Sterilization Mode' to gather all the straw cups and wash them every three days. People usually use a lot of water to wash dishes thoroughly, but since the dishwasher is consistent, the bill actually decreases. How to clean the dishwasher: I put citric acid in the detergent dispenser and run it on the drum wash cycle. Comments (English): [ 1-Year Usage Review ] || ---------------- || 1-Year Usage Review. Purchase Date: April 30, 2024. Hello, I am a housewife of 10 years raising a 40-month-old child and a member of a 3-person household. I have used this for a year and am finally leaving a review now. This is an honest review based on my own purchase and long-term use. First, although we graduated from baby bottles a long time ago, washing straw cups was too difficult. As my child grew, dishes, water bottles, and bowls piled up so much that washing dishes became a major chore. However, buying a large dishwasher wasn't an option because our kitchen is on the smaller side, and built-in models were out of the question. So, I did a lot of searching online. Based on my consideration and experience, here is the conclusion: Does it clean well? = I wanted to put everything in at once and wash it thoroughly. As shown in the picture, I always load a lot of items for washing, and it cleans up nicely. Previously, I used a basket, but it felt like straws weren't getting cleaned properly. However, when I put the straws directly into the existing dishwasher, they actually cleaned much better. Even if you pack everything like Tetris, it cleans sufficiently well. Design. What more needs to be said? It’s not that big, and the color is lovely pink. I’ve been using it for a year, and it’s so pretty with its glossy finish and not a single scratch. Visitors who see it in person also say how beautiful it is and ask if it’s really a dishwasher. Does it dry? = When I bought it, I thought it dried immediately after washing, but that wasn't the case. Instead, there is a separate drying mode, but it doesn't dry things completely and feels a bit iffy. Since I'm not going to use it right away anyway, I just leave it completely open and let it dry on its own, so I haven't really needed the drying function and have been using it well for a year. However, I do feel a bit uneasy about baby bottles, children's tableware, and straws, so I use the 'Baby Bottle Sterilization Mode' to gather all the straw cups and wash them every three days. Is it convenient? = For a year, the only dishwashing I do is frying pans. I run everything, stainless steel and all. I bought it for convenience, and I am completely satisfied. It’s perfect for a household of three. Even though I have a lot of dishes to wash, I run it about twice a day. I've never run it more than three times; it's usually twice. Also, having a separate basket for cutlery is definitely a plus. I've never had anything fly off. Does it increase water bills? = My water bill dropped significantly after using the dishwasher. People usually use a lot of water to wash dishes thoroughly, but since the dishwasher is consistent, the bill actually decreases. How to clean the dishwasher: I put citric acid in the detergent dispenser and run it on the drum wash cycle. I remove the filter at the bottom, soak it in warm water, and then clean it with a toothbrush. It keeps things clean and isn't difficult. I haven't bought any separate cleaning detergent. Another good point is that if you get extra dishes in the middle of the cycle, you can stop it, open the lid, and put them in. (Please refer to the photo; water doesn't leak.) Also, there is an automatic opening function, so it stays slightly open after the cycle is finished, allowing for natural drying. I tend to open it completely to dry. After using it for a year, I realized that even the parts I initially considered downsides are actually strengths. I am still very satisfied and using it well. If my review was helpful, please give it a thumbs up.

Comments (English): [ 1-Year Usage Review ] || ---------------- || 1-Year Usage Review. Purchase Date: April 30, 2024. Hello, I am a housewife of 10 years raising a 40-month-old child and a member of a 3-person household. I have used this for a year and am finally leaving a review now. This is an honest review based on my own purchase and long-term use. First, although we graduated from baby bottles a long time ago, washing straw cups was too difficult. As my child grew, dishes, water bottles, and bowls piled up so much that washing dishes became a major chore. However, buying a large dishwasher wasn't an option because our kitchen is on the smaller side, and built-in models were out of the question. So, I did a lot of searching online. Based on my consideration and experience, here is the conclusion: Does it clean well? = I wanted to put everything in at once and wash it thoroughly. As shown in the picture, I always load a lot of items for washing, and it cleans up nicely. Previously, I used a basket, but it felt like straws weren't getting cleaned properly. However, when I put the straws directly into the existing dishwasher, they actually cleaned much better. Even if you pack everything like Tetris, it cleans sufficiently well. Design. What more needs to be said? It’s not that big, and the color is lovely pink. I’ve been using it for a year, and it’s so pretty with its glossy finish and not a single scratch. Visitors who see it in person also say how beautiful it is and ask if it’s really a dishwasher. Does it dry? = When I bought it, I thought it dried immediately after washing, but that wasn't the case. Instead, there is a separate drying mode, but it doesn't dry things completely and feels a bit iffy. Since I'm not going to use it right away anyway, I just leave it completely open and let it dry on its own, so I haven't really needed the drying function and have been using it well for a year. However, I do feel a bit uneasy about baby bottles, children's tableware, and straws, so I use the 'Baby Bottle Sterilization Mode' to gather all the straw cups and wash them every three days. Is it convenient? = For a year, the only dishwashing I do is frying pans. I run everything, stainless steel and all. I bought it for convenience, and I am completely satisfied. It’s perfect for a household of three. Even though I have a lot of dishes to wash, I run it about twice a day. I've never run it more than three times; it's usually twice. Also, having a separate basket for cutlery is definitely a plus. I've never had anything fly off. Does it increase water bills? = My water bill dropped significantly after using the dishwasher. People usually use a lot of water to wash dishes thoroughly, but since the dishwasher is consistent, the bill actually decreases. How to clean the dishwasher: I put citric acid in the detergent dispenser and run it on the drum wash cycle. I remove the filter at the bottom, soak it in warm water, and then clean it with a toothbrush. It keeps things clean and isn't difficult. I haven't bought any separate cleaning detergent. Another good point is that if you get extra dishes in the middle of the cycle, you can stop it, open the lid, and put them in. (Please refer to the photo; water doesn't leak.) Also, there is an automatic opening function, so it stays slightly open after the cycle is finished, allowing for natural drying. I tend to open it completely to dry. After using it for a year, I realized that even the parts I initially considered downsides are actually strengths. I am still very satisfied and using it well. If my review was helpful, please give it a thumbs up.

Comments (English): [ 1-Year Usage Review ] || ---------------- || 1-Year Usage Review. Purchase Date: April 30, 2024. Hello, I am a housewife of 10 years raising a 40-month-old child and a member of a 3-person household. I have used this for a year and am finally leaving a review now. This is an honest review based on my own purchase and long-term use. First, although we graduated from baby bottles a long time ago, washing straw cups was too difficult. As my child grew, dishes, water bottles, and bowls piled up so much that washing dishes became a major chore. However, buying a large dishwasher wasn't an option because our kitchen is on the smaller side, and built-in models were out of the question. So, I did a lot of searching online. Based on my consideration and experience, here is the conclusion: Does it clean well? = I wanted to put everything in at once and wash it thoroughly. As shown in the picture, I always load a lot of items for washing, and it cleans up nicely. Previously, I used a basket, but it felt like straws weren't getting cleaned properly. However, when I put the straws directly into the existing dishwasher, they actually cleaned much better. Even if you pack everything like Tetris, it cleans sufficiently well. Design. What more needs to be said? It’s not that big, and the color is lovely pink. I’ve been using it for a year, and it’s so pretty with its glossy finish and not a single scratch. Visitors who see it in person also say how beautiful it is and ask if it’s really a dishwasher. Does it dry? = When I bought it, I thought it dried immediately after washing, but that wasn't the case. Instead, there is a separate drying mode, but it doesn't dry things completely and feels a bit iffy. Since I'm not going to use it right away anyway, I just leave it completely open and let it dry on its own, so I haven't really needed the drying function and have been using it well for a year. However, I do feel a bit uneasy about baby bottles, children's tableware, and straws, so I use the 'Baby Bottle Sterilization Mode' to gather all the straw cups and wash them every three days. Is it convenient? = For a year, the only dishwashing I do is frying pans. I run everything, stainless steel and all. I bought it for convenience, and I am completely satisfied. It’s perfect for a household of three. Even though I have a lot of dishes to wash, I run it about twice a day. I've never run it more than three times; it's usually twice. Also, having a separate basket for cutlery is definitely a plus. I've never had anything fly off. Does it increase water bills? = My water bill dropped significantly after using the dishwasher. People usually use a lot of water to wash dishes thoroughly, but since the dishwasher is consistent, the bill actually decreases. How to clean the dishwasher: I put citric acid in the detergent dispenser and run it on the drum wash cycle. I remove the filter at the bottom, soak it in warm water, and then clean it with a toothbrush. It keeps things clean and isn't difficult. I haven't bought any separate cleaning detergent. Another good point is that if you get extra dishes in the middle of the cycle, you can stop it, open the lid, and put them in. (Please refer to the photo; water doesn't leak.) Also, there is an automatic opening function, so it stays slightly open after the cycle is finished, allowing for natural drying. I tend to open it completely to dry. After using it for a year, I realized that even the parts I initially considered downsides are actually strengths. I am still very satisfied and using it well. If my review was helpful, please give it a thumbs up.

Comments (English): [ 1-Year Usage Review ] || ---------------- || 1-Year Usage Review. Purchase Date: April 30, 2024. Hello, I am a housewife of 10 years raising a 40-month-old child and a member of a 3-person household. I have used this for a year and am finally leaving a review now. This is an honest review based on my own purchase and long-term use. First, although we graduated from baby bottles a long time ago, washing straw cups was too difficult. As my child grew, dishes, water bottles, and bowls piled up so much that washing dishes became a major chore. However, buying a large dishwasher wasn't an option because our kitchen is on the smaller side, and built-in models were out of the question. So, I did a lot of searching online. Based on my consideration and experience, here is the conclusion: Does it clean well? = I wanted to put everything in at once and wash it thoroughly. As shown in the picture, I always load a lot of items for washing, and it cleans up nicely. Previously, I used a basket, but it felt like straws weren't getting cleaned properly. However, when I put the straws directly into the existing dishwasher, they actually cleaned much better. Even if you pack everything like Tetris, it cleans sufficiently well. Design. What more needs to be said? It’s not that big, and the color is lovely pink. I’ve been using it for a year, and it’s so pretty with its glossy finish and not a single scratch. Visitors who see it in person also say how beautiful it is and ask if it’s really a dishwasher. Does it dry? = When I bought it, I thought it dried immediately after washing, but that wasn't the case. Instead, there is a separate drying mode, but it doesn't dry things completely and feels a bit iffy. Since I'm not going to use it right away anyway, I just leave it completely open and let it dry on its own, so I haven't really needed the drying function and have been using it well for a year. However, I do feel a bit uneasy about baby bottles, children's tableware, and straws, so I use the 'Baby Bottle Sterilization Mode' to gather all the straw cups and wash them every three days. Is it convenient? = For a year, the only dishwashing I do is frying pans. I run everything, stainless steel and all. I bought it for convenience, and I am completely satisfied. It’s perfect for a household of three. Even though I have a lot of dishes to wash, I run it about twice a day. I've never run it more than three times; it's usually twice. Also, having a separate basket for cutlery is definitely a plus. I've never had anything fly off. Does it increase water bills? = My water bill dropped significantly after using the dishwasher. People usually use a lot of water to wash dishes thoroughly, but since the dishwasher is consistent, the bill actually decreases. How to clean the dishwasher: I put citric acid in the detergent dispenser and run it on the drum wash cycle. I remove the filter at the bottom, soak it in warm water, and then clean it with a toothbrush. It keeps things clean and isn't difficult. I haven't bought any separate cleaning detergent. Another good point is that if you get extra dishes in the middle of the cycle, you can stop it, open the lid, and put them in. (Please refer to the photo; water doesn't leak.) Also, there is an automatic opening function, so it stays slightly open after the cycle is finished, allowing for natural drying. I tend to open it completely to dry. After using it for a year, I realized that even the parts I initially considered downsides are actually strengths. I am still very satisfied and using it well. If my review was helpful, please give it a thumbs up.

Comments (English): [ 1-Year Usage Review ] || ---------------- || 1-Year Usage Review. Purchase Date: April 30, 2024. Hello, I am a housewife of 10 years raising a 40-month-old child and a member of a 3-person household. I have used this for a year and am finally leaving a review now. This is an honest review based on my own purchase and long-term use. First, although we graduated from baby bottles a long time ago, washing straw cups was too difficult. As my child grew, dishes, water bottles, and bowls piled up so much that washing dishes became a major chore. However, buying a large dishwasher wasn't an option because our kitchen is on the smaller side, and built-in models were out of the question. So, I did a lot of searching online. Based on my consideration and experience, here is the conclusion: Does it clean well? = I wanted to put everything in at once and wash it thoroughly. As shown in the picture, I always load a lot of items for washing, and it cleans up nicely. Previously, I used a basket, but it felt like straws weren't getting cleaned properly. However, when I put the straws directly into the existing dishwasher, they actually cleaned much better. Even if you pack everything like Tetris, it cleans sufficiently well. Design. What more needs to be said? It’s not that big, and the color is lovely pink. I’ve been using it for a year, and it’s so pretty with its glossy finish and not a single scratch. Visitors who see it in person also say how beautiful it is and ask if it’s really a dishwasher. Does it dry? = When I bought it, I thought it dried immediately after washing, but that wasn't the case. Instead, there is a separate drying mode, but it doesn't dry things completely and feels a bit iffy. Since I'm not going to use it right away anyway, I just leave it completely open and let it dry on its own, so I haven't really needed the drying function and have been using it well for a year. However, I do feel a bit uneasy about baby bottles, children's tableware, and straws, so I use the 'Baby Bottle Sterilization Mode' to gather all the straw cups and wash them every three days. Is it convenient? = For a year, the only dishwashing I do is frying pans. I run everything, stainless steel and all. I bought it for convenience, and I am completely satisfied. It’s perfect for a household of three. Even though I have a lot of dishes to wash, I run it about twice a day. I've never run it more than three times; it's usually twice. Also, having a separate basket for cutlery is definitely a plus. I've never had anything fly off. Does it increase water bills? = My water bill dropped significantly after using the dishwasher. People usually use a lot of water to wash dishes thoroughly, but since the dishwasher is consistent, the bill actually decreases. How to clean the dishwasher: I put citric acid in the detergent dispenser and run it on the drum wash cycle. I remove the filter at the bottom, soak it in warm water, and then clean it with a toothbrush. It keeps things clean and isn't difficult. I haven't bought any separate cleaning detergent. Another good point is that if you get extra dishes in the middle of the cycle, you can stop it, open the lid, and put them in. (Please refer to the photo; water doesn't leak.) Also, there is an automatic opening function, so it stays slightly open after the cycle is finished, allowing for natural drying. I tend to open it completely to dry. After using it for a year, I realized that even the parts I initially considered downsides are actually strengths. I am still very satisfied and using it well. If my review was helpful, please give it a thumbs up.

Comments (English): [ 1-Year Usage Review ] || ---------------- || 1-Year Usage Review. Purchase Date: April 30, 2024. Hello, I am a housewife of 10 years raising a 40-month-old child and a member of a 3-person household. I have used this for a year and am finally leaving a review now. This is an honest review based on my own purchase and long-term use. First, although we graduated from baby bottles a long time ago, washing straw cups was too difficult. As my child grew, dishes, water bottles, and bowls piled up so much that washing dishes became a major chore. However, buying a large dishwasher wasn't an option because our kitchen is on the smaller side, and built-in models were out of the question. So, I did a lot of searching online. Based on my consideration and experience, here is the conclusion: Does it clean well? = I wanted to put everything in at once and wash it thoroughly. As shown in the picture, I always load a lot of items for washing, and it cleans up nicely. Previously, I used a basket, but it felt like straws weren't getting cleaned properly. However, when I put the straws directly into the existing dishwasher, they actually cleaned much better. Even if you pack everything like Tetris, it cleans sufficiently well. Design. What more needs to be said? It’s not that big, and the color is lovely pink. I’ve been using it for a year, and it’s so pretty with its glossy finish and not a single scratch. Visitors who see it in person also say how beautiful it is and ask if it’s really a dishwasher. Does it dry? = When I bought it, I thought it dried immediately after washing, but that wasn't the case. Instead, there is a separate drying mode, but it doesn't dry things completely and feels a bit iffy. Since I'm not going to use it right away anyway, I just leave it completely open and let it dry on its own, so I haven't really needed the drying function and have been using it well for a year. However, I do feel a bit uneasy about baby bottles, children's tableware, and straws, so I use the 'Baby Bottle Sterilization Mode' to gather all the straw cups and wash them every three days. Is it convenient? = For a year, the only dishwashing I do is frying pans. I run everything, stainless steel and all. I bought it for convenience, and I am completely satisfied. It’s perfect for a household of three. Even though I have a lot of dishes to wash, I run it about twice a day. I've never run it more than three times; it's usually twice. Also, having a separate basket for cutlery is definitely a plus. I've never had anything fly off. Does it increase water bills? = My water bill dropped significantly after using the dishwasher. People usually use a lot of water to wash dishes thoroughly, but since the dishwasher is consistent, the bill actually decreases. How to clean the dishwasher: I put citric acid in the detergent dispenser and run it on the drum wash cycle. I remove the filter at the bottom, soak it in warm water, and then clean it with a toothbrush. It keeps things clean and isn't difficult. I haven't bought any separate cleaning detergent. Another good point is that if you get extra dishes in the middle of the cycle, you can stop it, open the lid, and put them in. (Please refer to the photo; water doesn't leak.) Also, there is an automatic opening function, so it stays slightly open after the cycle is finished, allowing for natural drying. I tend to open it completely to dry. After using it for a year, I realized that even the parts I initially considered downsides are actually strengths. I am still very satisfied and using it well. If my review was helpful, please give it a thumbs up.

Comments (English): [ 1-Year Usage Review ] || ---------------- || 1-Year Usage Review. Purchase Date: April 30, 2024. Hello, I am a housewife of 10 years raising a 40-month-old child and a member of a 3-person household. I have used this for a year and am finally leaving a review now. This is an honest review based on my own purchase and long-term use. First, although we graduated from baby bottles a long time ago, washing straw cups was too difficult. As my child grew, dishes, water bottles, and bowls piled up so much that washing dishes became a major chore. However, buying a large dishwasher wasn't an option because our kitchen is on the smaller side, and built-in models were out of the question. So, I did a lot of searching online. Based on my consideration and experience, here is the conclusion: Does it clean well? = I wanted to put everything in at once and wash it thoroughly. As shown in the picture, I always load a lot of items for washing, and it cleans up nicely. Previously, I used a basket, but it felt like straws weren't getting cleaned properly. However, when I put the straws directly into the existing dishwasher, they actually cleaned much better. Even if you pack everything like Tetris, it cleans sufficiently well. Design. What more needs to be said? It’s not that big, and the color is lovely pink. I’ve been using it for a year, and it’s so pretty with its glossy finish and not a single scratch. Visitors who see it in person also say how beautiful it is and ask if it’s really a dishwasher. Does it dry? = When I bought it, I thought it dried immediately after washing, but that wasn't the case. Instead, there is a separate drying mode, but it doesn't dry things completely and feels a bit iffy. Since I'm not going to use it right away anyway, I just leave it completely open and let it dry on its own, so I haven't really needed the drying function and have been using it well for a year. However, I do feel a bit uneasy about baby bottles, children's tableware, and straws, so I use the 'Baby Bottle Sterilization Mode' to gather all the straw cups and wash them every three days. Is it convenient? = For a year, the only dishwashing I do is frying pans. I run everything, stainless steel and all. I bought it for convenience, and I am completely satisfied. It’s perfect for a household of three. Even though I have a lot of dishes to wash, I run it about twice a day. I've never run it more than three times; it's usually twice. Also, having a separate basket for cutlery is definitely a plus. I've never had anything fly off. Does it increase water bills? = My water bill dropped significantly after using the dishwasher. People usually use a lot of water to wash dishes thoroughly, but since the dishwasher is consistent, the bill actually decreases. How to clean the dishwasher: I put citric acid in the detergent dispenser and run it on the drum wash cycle. I remove the filter at the bottom, soak it in warm water, and then clean it with a toothbrush. It keeps things clean and isn't difficult. I haven't bought any separate cleaning detergent. Another good point is that if you get extra dishes in the middle of the cycle, you can stop it, open the lid, and put them in. (Please refer to the photo; water doesn't leak.) Also, there is an automatic opening function, so it stays slightly open after the cycle is finished, allowing for natural drying. I tend to open it completely to dry. After using it for a year, I realized that even the parts I initially considered downsides are actually strengths. I am still very satisfied and using it well. If my review was helpful, please give it a thumbs up.

Sentence (English): As a two-person household, the appliance I had my eye on before moving into my new home was a dishwasher.
Comments (English): As a two-person household, the appliance I had my eye on before moving into my new home was a dishwasher. You might wonder how much dishwashing a two-person household can do, but we are a family that thinks hygiene is really, really important, so we put side dishes on plates with washed chopsticks and eat them, and we wash and use cooking utensils alternately when cooking, so we are proud that the dishwashing is more than the average three-person household. I wanted to have some free time even in this busy modern society. They say it doesn’t take long to wash dishes, but is the time it takes to put them in the dishwasher all at once the same as the time it takes to lather the dish sponge, wash the dishes, and dry them on the shelf? Thanks to the dishwasher, I can do other housework or have free time to sit down and watch movies or dramas while drinking coffee. Since it is a rented house, I couldn’t just bring in built-in appliances, so I bought a countertop product. The biggest concerns I had were the capacity and the fact that it didn’t have an automatic door opening, making it vulnerable to mold and bacteria. For a two-person household, our house uses a lot of dishes, and the most I've ever put in was 22 plates. At first, I was half-confident that it wouldn't be cleaned well, but it was much cleaner and more shiny than if someone had washed it. Just because it's for two people, you can't ignore the capacity. And in particular, many people talked about the automatic door opening function, and I also thought, "Why doesn't this product have an automatic door opening?" But when I actually used it, it was a product that didn't need the door to open automatically. If you select the UV sterilization and hot air drying options, the moisture from the washed dishes is blown away, and the UV lamp kills mold and bacteria, so the automatic door opening function was not necessary in the first place. This was the part I was most worried about, but I felt that LG had done a lot of research on this part. I was also very satisfied with the delivery service, and I was especially worried that it would be noisy because it was early in the morning, but the installation was done quietly, and I was happy that they even did the final cleanup and provided a friendly explanation.
Comments (Original): 2인 가구 기준으로 신혼 집 이사 가기 전부터 눈독 들이던 가전이 식기세척기였습니다.2인 가구가 설거지 거리 나와봐야 얼마나 나오느냐? 하시겠지만, 저희는 위생이 정말 정말 중요하다고 생각하는 가정이어서 반찬도 하나하나 씻어낸 젓가락으로 접시에 담아 먹고, 요리를 할 때에도 조리 도구를 번갈아 씻으며 사용하기 때문에 설거지 거리가 보통 3인 가족 이상으로 나온다고 자부해요.바쁜 현대 사회 속에서도 여유 시간을 갖고 싶었어요.설거지 얼마 안 걸린다고 하지만, 식기 세척기에 한 번에 넣고 돌리는 시간이랑 일일이 수세미에 거품 내고 접시 닦고 선반에 말리는 시간이랑 과연 같을까요? 식기 세척기가 들어 온 덕분에 다른 집안일을 하거나 여유 시간을 틈타 커피를 마시면서 영화나 드라마를 보면서 앉아있는 시간이 생겨 가장 행복합니다.전세집이라서 함부로 빌트인 가전을 들일 수 없어 카운터 탑 제품을 구매했는데, 가장 우려되는 부분은 용량과 자동 문 열림이 없어 곰팡이나 세균에 취약한 부분이었어요.2인 가구 치고는 저희 집은 접시를 많이 사용하는 편인데, 가장 많이 넣어 본 접시가 22개였어요. 처음에는 잘 안닦이겠거니 하고 반신반의 한 채로 세척을 진행했는데 웬걸, 사람이 설거지 한 것보다 훨씬 깔끔하고 반짝반짝하게 닦여있더라구요. 2인용이라고 해서 용량 무시할 게 못되더라구요.그리고 특히 자동 문 열림 기능에 대해서 사람들이 말이 많으셨는데 저 또한 이 제품에 왜 자동 문 열림이 없을까? 라고 생각했었어요. 그런데 실제로 사용 해 보니 자동으로 문이 열릴 필요가 없는 제품이었어요. UV살균과 열풍 건조 옵션을 선택하면 세척 된 식기의 물기를 날려주고 UV램프가 곰팡이균, 세균까지 잡아주었기 때문에 자동 문 열림 기능이 애초에 필요가 없었던 것입니다. 가장 걱정스러웠던 부분인데 LG에서 이런 부분에 대해서도 굉장히 연구를 많이 했구나 라는 걸 느꼈습니다.배송 서비스도 굉장히 만족스러웠고, 특히 이른 아침 시간이어서 소음이 나지는 않을까 걱정했는데 조용하게 설치가 잘 이루어졌고 마무리 정리와 친절한 설명까지 진행해주셔서 좋았습니다.

Sentence (English): I wanted to have some free time even in this busy modern society.
Comments (English): As a two-person household, the appliance I had my eye on before moving into my new home was a dishwasher. You might wonder how much dishwashing a two-person household can do, but we are a family that thinks hygiene is really, really important, so we put side dishes on plates with washed chopsticks and eat them, and we wash and use cooking utensils alternately when cooking, so we are proud that the dishwashing is more than the average three-person household. I wanted to have some free time even in this busy modern society. They say it doesn’t take long to wash dishes, but is the time it takes to put them in the dishwasher all at once the same as the time it takes to lather the dish sponge, wash the dishes, and dry them on the shelf? Thanks to the dishwasher, I can do other housework or have free time to sit down and watch movies or dramas while drinking coffee. Since it is a rented house, I couldn’t just bring in built-in appliances, so I bought a countertop product. The biggest concerns I had were the capacity and the fact that it didn’t have an automatic door opening, making it vulnerable to mold and bacteria. For a two-person household, our house uses a lot of dishes, and the most I've ever put in was 22 plates. At first, I was half-confident that it wouldn't be cleaned well, but it was much cleaner and more shiny than if someone had washed it. Just because it's for two people, you can't ignore the capacity. And in particular, many people talked about the automatic door opening function, and I also thought, "Why doesn't this product have an automatic door opening?" But when I actually used it, it was a product that didn't need the door to open automatically. If you select the UV sterilization and hot air drying options, the moisture from the washed dishes is blown away, and the UV lamp kills mold and bacteria, so the automatic door opening function was not necessary in the first place. This was the part I was most worried about, but I felt that LG had done a lot of research on this part. I was also very satisfied with the delivery service, and I was especially worried that it would be noisy because it was early in the morning, but the installation was done quietly, and I was happy that they even did the final cleanup and provided a friendly explanation.

Sentence (English): Thanks to the dishwasher, I can do other housework or have free time to sit down and watch movies or dramas while drinking coffee.
Comments (English): As a two-person household, the appliance I had my eye on before moving into my new home was a dishwasher. You might wonder how much dishwashing a two-person household can do, but we are a family that thinks hygiene is really, really important, so we put side dishes on plates with washed chopsticks and eat them, and we wash and use cooking utensils alternately when cooking, so we are proud that the dishwashing is more than the average three-person household. I wanted to have some free time even in this busy modern society. They say it doesn’t take long to wash dishes, but is the time it takes to put them in the dishwasher all at once the same as the time it takes to lather the dish sponge, wash the dishes, and dry them on the shelf? Thanks to the dishwasher, I can do other housework or have free time to sit down and watch movies or dramas while drinking coffee. Since it is a rented house, I couldn’t just bring in built-in appliances, so I bought a countertop product. The biggest concerns I had were the capacity and the fact that it didn’t have an automatic door opening, making it vulnerable to mold and bacteria. For a two-person household, our house uses a lot of dishes, and the most I've ever put in was 22 plates. At first, I was half-confident that it wouldn't be cleaned well, but it was much cleaner and more shiny than if someone had washed it. Just because it's for two people, you can't ignore the capacity. And in particular, many people talked about the automatic door opening function, and I also thought, "Why doesn't this product have an automatic door opening?" But when I actually used it, it was a product that didn't need the door to open automatically. If you select the UV sterilization and hot air drying options, the moisture from the washed dishes is blown away, and the UV lamp kills mold and bacteria, so the automatic door opening function was not necessary in the first place. This was the part I was most worried about, but I felt that LG had done a lot of research on this part. I was also very satisfied with the delivery service, and I was especially worried that it would be noisy because it was early in the morning, but the installation was done quietly, and I was happy that they even did the final cleanup and provided a friendly explanation.

Comments (English): As a two-person household, the appliance I had my eye on before moving into my new home was a dishwasher. I wanted to have some free time even in this busy modern society. They say it doesn’t take long to wash dishes, but is the time it takes to put them in the dishwasher all at once the same as the time it takes to lather the dish sponge, wash the dishes, and dry them on the shelf? Since it is a rented house, I couldn’t just bring in built-in appliances, so I bought a countertop product. The biggest concerns I had were the capacity and the fact that it didn’t have an automatic door opening, making it vulnerable to mold and bacteria. For a two-person household, our house uses a lot of dishes, and the most I've ever put in was 22 plates. This was the part I was most worried about, but I felt that LG had done a lot of research on this part. Sentence (English): Just because it's for two people, you can't ignore the capacity.
Comments (English): As a two-person household, the appliance I had my eye on before moving into my new home was a dishwasher. You might wonder how much dishwashing a two-person household can do, but we are a family that thinks hygiene is really, really important, so we put side dishes on plates with washed chopsticks and eat them, and we wash and use cooking utensils alternately when cooking, so we are proud that the dishwashing is more than the average three-person household. I wanted to have some free time even in this busy modern society. They say it doesn’t take long to wash dishes, but is the time it takes to put them in the dishwasher all at once the same as the time it takes to lather the dish sponge, wash the dishes, and dry them on the shelf? Thanks to the dishwasher, I can do other housework or have free time to sit down and watch movies or dramas while drinking coffee. Since it is a rented house, I couldn’t just bring in built-in appliances, so I bought a countertop product. The biggest concerns I had were the capacity and the fact that it didn’t have an automatic door opening, making it vulnerable to mold and bacteria. For a two-person household, our house uses a lot of dishes, and the most I've ever put in was 22 plates. At first, I was half-confident that it wouldn't be cleaned well, but it was much cleaner and more shiny than if someone had washed it. Just because it's for two people, you can't ignore the capacity. And in particular, many people talked about the automatic door opening function, and I also thought, "Why doesn't this product have an automatic door opening?" But when I actually used it, it was a product that didn't need the door to open automatically. If you select the UV sterilization and hot air drying options, the moisture from the washed dishes is blown away, and the UV lamp kills mold and bacteria, so the automatic door opening function was not necessary in the first place. This was the part I was most worried about, but I felt that LG had done a lot of research on this part. I was also very satisfied with the delivery service, and I was especially worried that it would be noisy because it was early in the morning, but the installation was done quietly, and I was happy that they even did the final cleanup and provided a friendly explanation.

Comments (English): As a two-person household, the appliance I had my eye on before moving into my new home was a dishwasher. I wanted to have some free time even in this busy modern society. Comments (English): As a two-person household, the appliance I had my eye on before moving into my new home was a dishwasher. You might wonder how much dishwashing a two-person household can do, but we are a family that thinks hygiene is really, really important, so we put side dishes on plates with washed chopsticks and eat them, and we wash and use cooking utensils alternately when cooking, so we are proud that the dishwashing is more than the average three-person household. I wanted to have some free time even in this busy modern society. They say it doesn’t take long to wash dishes, but is the time it takes to put them in the dishwasher all at once the same as the time it takes to lather the dish sponge, wash the dishes, and dry them on the shelf? Thanks to the dishwasher, I can do other housework or have free time to sit down and watch movies or dramas while drinking coffee. Since it is a rented house, I couldn’t just bring in built-in appliances, so I bought a countertop product. The biggest concerns I had were the capacity and the fact that it didn’t have an automatic door opening, making it vulnerable to mold and bacteria. For a two-person household, our house uses a lot of dishes, and the most I've ever put in was 22 plates. At first, I was half-confident that it wouldn't be cleaned well, but it was much cleaner and more shiny than if someone had washed it. Just because it's for two people, you can't ignore the capacity. And in particular, many people talked about the automatic door opening function, and I also thought, "Why doesn't this product have an automatic door opening?" But when I actually used it, it was a product that didn't need the door to open automatically. If you select the UV sterilization and hot air drying options, the moisture from the washed dishes is blown away, and the UV lamp kills mold and bacteria, so the automatic door opening function was not necessary in the first place. This was the part I was most worried about, but I felt that LG had done a lot of research on this part. I was also very satisfied with the delivery service, and I was especially worried that it would be noisy because it was early in the morning, but the installation was done quietly, and I was happy that they even did the final cleanup and provided a friendly explanation.

Cons: Dishes still aren't dry enough to put in cabinets, especially plastics, even with the extended dry function. Dumping off water and putting the dishes in a dish drainer to air dry should not still be a thing. The silverware basket is huge and takes up room that could be used for other dishes. I am still using my silverware baskets from my old dishwasher from 20 years ago.

Comments (English): [ Broke after two uses! ] || ---------------- || I am extremely disappointed in this dishwasher and with Lowe's in general. I bought it in store with the delivery package. Lowe's was offering a $200 rebate on dishwashers with installation $599.00 and up. Delivery and installation took two weeks which I found a bit ridiculous, but I dealt with it. The dishwasher was installed and worked fine for the first two times. On the third attempt, the dishwasher would make a few sounds, then the lights would flash and the control panel would lock and not allow it to reset or to allow any input. I did the troubleshooting steps of unplugging and waiting, then plugging back in and retrying. This would reset the dishwasher (allow inputs into the control panel) but would also reset the cycle of failure. I called the help center and was told to redo my troubleshooting steps despite having already done them several times. At one point, it appeared to start working. The customer service rep told me that after speaking with a tech, if they came out to look at it and it was working, I would be charged. After hanging up with customer service, the dishwasher again failed to complete the cycle. I had to schedule a service tech to come to my house. This dishwasher was purchased on 8/29/24. It is now 10/07/24 and the service tech is supposed to come today. They were also supposed to call last night to confirm they'd be here but I never got a call. I had to go online to confirm that I did indeed have a service scheduled for today. To add insult to injury, my rebate was denied despite meeting all of the requirements and giving all of the information requested. twice. Calls to the rebate center resulted in over 30 minutes of being on hold before finally requesting a call back. I'm extremely disappointed in this whole process,

Sentence (English): As a two-person household, the appliance I had my eye on before moving into my new home was a dishwasher.
Comments (English): [ Moving into a newlywed home for a two-person household ] || ---------------- || As a two-person household, the appliance I had my eye on before moving into my new home was a dishwasher. You might wonder how much dishwashing a two-person household can do, but we are a family that thinks hygiene is really, really important, so we put side dishes on plates with washed chopsticks and eat them, and we wash and use cooking utensils alternately when cooking, so we are proud that the dishwashing is more than the average three-person household. I wanted to have some free time even in this busy modern society. They say it doesn’t take long to wash dishes, but is the time it takes to put them in the dishwasher all at once the same as the time it takes to lather the dish sponge, wash the dishes, and dry them on the shelf? Thanks to the dishwasher, I can do other housework or have free time to sit down and watch movies or dramas while drinking coffee. Since it is a rented house, I couldn’t just bring in built-in appliances, so I bought a countertop product. The biggest concerns I had were the capacity and the fact that it doesn’t have an automatic door opening, making it vulnerable to mold and bacteria. For a two-person household, our house uses a lot of dishes, and the most I've ever put in was 22 plates. At first, I was half-confident that it wouldn't be cleaned well, but it was much cleaner and more shiny than when someone washed it. Just because it's for two people, you can't ignore the capacity. And in particular, many people talked about the automatic door opening function, and I also thought, "Why doesn't this product have an automatic door opening?" But when I actually used it, it was a product that didn't need the door to open automatically. If you select the UV sterilization and hot air drying options, the moisture from the washed dishes is blown away, and the UV lamp kills mold and bacteria, so the automatic door opening function was not necessary in the first place. This was the part I was most worried about, but I felt that LG had done a lot of research on this part. I was also very satisfied with the delivery service, and I was especially worried that it would be noisy because it was early in the morning, but the installation was done quietly, and I was happy that they even did the final cleanup and provided a friendly explanation.
Comments (Original): [ 2인 가구 기준으로 신혼 집 이사 가 ] || ---------------- || 2인 가구 기준으로 신혼 집 이사 가기 전부터 눈독 들이던 가전이 식기세척기였습니다.2인 가구가 설거지 거리 나와봐야 얼마나 나오느냐? 하시겠지만, 저희는 위생이 정말 정말 중요하다고 생각하는 가정이어서 반찬도 하나하나 씻어낸 젓가락으로 접시에 담아 먹고, 요리를 할 때에도 조리 도구를 번갈아 씻으며 사용하기 때문에 설거지 거리가 보통 3인 가족 이상으로 나온다고 자부해요.바쁜 현대 사회 속에서도 여유 시간을 갖고 싶었어요.설거지 얼마 안 걸린다고 하지만, 식기 세척기에 한 번에 넣고 돌리는 시간이랑 일일이 수세미에 거품 내고 접시 닦고 선반에 말리는 시간이랑 과연 같을까요? 식기 세척기가 들어 온 덕분에 다른 집안일을 하거나 여유 시간을 틈타 커피를 마시면서 영화나 드라마를 보면서 앉아있는 시간이 생겨 가장 행복합니다.전세집이라서 함부로 빌트인 가전을 들일 수 없어 카운터 탑 제품을 구매했는데, 가장 우려되는 부분은 용량과 자동 문 열림이 없어 곰팡이나 세균에 취약한 부분이었어요.2인 가구 치고는 저희 집은 접시를 많이 사용하는 편인데, 가장 많이 넣어 본 접시가 22개였어요. 처음에는 잘 안닦이겠거니 하고 반신반의 한 채로 세척을 진행했는데 웬걸, 사람이 설거지 한 것보다 훨씬 깔끔하고 반짝반짝하게 닦여있더라구요. 2인용이라고 해서 용량 무시할 게 못되더라구요.그리고 특히 자동 문 열림 기능에 대해서 사람들이 말이 많으셨는데 저 또한 이 제품에 왜 자동 문 열림이 없을까? 라고 생각했었어요. 그런데 실제로 사용 해 보니 자동으로 문이 열릴 필요가 없는 제품이었어요. UV살균과 열풍 건조 옵션을 선택하면 세척 된 식기의 물기를 날려주고 UV램프가 곰팡이균, 세균까지 잡아주었기 때문에 자동 문 열림 기능이 애초에 필요가 없었던 것입니다. 가장 걱정스러웠던 부분인데 LG에서 이런 부분에 대해서도 굉장히 연구를 많이 했구나 라는 걸 느꼈습니다.배송 서비스도 굉장히 만족스러웠고, 특히 이른 아침 시간이어서 소음이 나지는 않을까 걱정했는데 조용하게 설치가 잘 이루어졌고 마무리 정리와 친절한 설명까지 진행해주셔서 좋았습니다.

You might wonder how much dishwashing a two-person household can do, but we are a family that thinks hygiene is really, really important, so we put side dishes on plates with washed chopsticks and eat them, and we wash and use cooking utensils alternately when cooking, so we are proud that the dishwashing is more than the average three-person household. I wanted to have some free time even in this busy modern society. They say it doesn’t take long to wash dishes, but is the time it takes to put them in the dishwasher all at once the same as the time it takes to lather the dish sponge, wash the dishes, and dry them on the shelf? Thanks to the dishwasher, I can do other housework or have free time to sit down and watch movies or dramas while drinking coffee. Since it is a rented house, I couldn’t just bring in built-in appliances, so I bought a countertop product. The biggest concerns I had were the capacity and the fact that it doesn’t have an automatic door opening, making it vulnerable to mold and bacteria. For a two-person household, our house uses a lot of dishes, and the most I've ever put in was 22 plates. At first, I was half-confident that it wouldn't be cleaned well, but it was much cleaner and more shiny than when someone washed it. Just because it's for two people, you can't ignore the capacity. And in particular, many people talked about the automatic door opening function, and I also thought, "Why doesn't this product have an automatic door opening?" But when I actually used it, it was a product that didn't need the door to open automatically. If you select the UV sterilization and hot air drying options, the moisture from the washed dishes is blown away, and the UV lamp kills mold and bacteria, so the automatic door opening function was not necessary in the first place. This was the part I was most worried about, but I felt that LG had done a lot of research on this part. I was also very satisfied with the delivery service, and I was especially worried that it would be noisy because it was early in the morning, but the installation was done quietly, and I was happy that they even did the final cleanup and provided a friendly explanation.

UV살균과 열풍 건조 옵션을 선택하면 세척 된 식기의 물기를 날려주고 UV램프가 곰팡이균, 세균까지 잡아주었기 때문에 자동 문 열림 기능이 애초에 필요가 없었던 것입니다. 가장 걱정스러웠던 부분인데 LG에서 이런 부분에 대해서도 굉장히 연구를 많이 했구나 라는 걸 느꼈습니다.배송 서비스도 굉장히 만족스러웠고, 특히 이른 아침 시간이어서 소음이 나지는 않을까 걱정했는데 조용하게 설치가 잘 이루어졌고 마무리 정리와 친절한 설명까지 진행해주셔서 좋았습니다.
